concept.reason: Actual postcranial photos and scaled reconstruction plus same-species skull/mandible comparisons are sufficient. No extra concept image.

scope: Whole living Nothosaurus mirabilis, proportions anchored to postcranial holotype UMO1000 with same-species skull comparisons. Reconstructed missing anatomy is explicit, not a single complete pristine skeleton or specimen scan.

scientific_limits.en: UMO1000 is a not fully grown incomplete skeleton: skull, shoulder girdle, posterior dorsals and distal tail are missing. Published restored total2.9–3.2m and inferred skull0.32m are estimates, not measurements of a complete animal. Skull photograph has no verified accession or restoration history; use it with actual SMNS59817 mandibular comparison, not as the holotype skull. Webbing, skin, color, complete feet, body thickness and missing tail tip are inferred. Do not copy N.giganteus, N.jagisteus, Simosaurus or modern sea-turtle fins.
scientific_limits.zh: UMO1000为未完全长成的不完整骨架，头骨、肩带、后躯干及末尾缺失。发表的补全总长2.9至3.2米及推测头长0.32米不是完整动物实测。头骨照片未核定编号与修复史，须结合SMNS59817真下颌比较，不冒充模式头骨。蹼、皮肤、颜色、完整脚形、软体厚度及尾尖推定；不得移植其他种属或海龟鳍。

original_scope.en: Planned animal asset: long fang-bearing head, sinuous neck and webbed limb plan.
original_scope.zh: 规划中的动物资产：长獠齿头、蜿蜒颈与蹼肢构型。

evidence_anchors.skeleton: Klein et al2022 actual Fig4 UMO1000 photographs20cm scale; Fig5 interpretative drawing. Fig3 historical cast is not original preserved full anatomy. Complete19-cervical neck,20 anterior dorsals, anterior caudal strings, humeri and right femur; posterior axial gaps explicit.
evidence_anchors.scale: 2022 body-size section: preserved axial strings212cm, inferred missing posterior dorsals23.5cm, estimated skull32cm and missing terminal tail20–50cm; authors estimate total290–320cm. Fig19 is a scaled RECONSTRUCTION, not photograph or independently measured whole specimen.
evidence_anchors.limbs: 2022 original humerus broad/wing-shaped and ulna flat; humerus-ulna ratio2.09. Femur comparatively slender with round-oval section. Digit/web envelope reconstruction conservative; no fossil skin claim.
evidence_anchors.head: Ghedoghedo2013 Tuebingen skull image attributed N.mirabilis shows long narrowed rostrum with anterior expansion and prominent pointed teeth. Rieppel1994 Fig3C actual N.mirabilis SMNS59817 symphysis20mm confirms elongate mandibular symphysis distinct from Fig3A Simosaurus. Neither is UMO1000 skull.
evidence_anchors.motion: 2022 large intercentral spaces and axial morphology support lateral undulation. Gentle lateral neck curve is plausible pose, not preserved fixed S-neck or demonstrated extreme flexibility.

scale.interpretation: Targets except explicitly preserved length are estimates chosen inside published restored range, not individual measurements. Curved pose reduces straight bounding-box length. Head and neck use published Fig19 estimates; remaining volumes/limbs simplified conservatively.

morphology: Elongate low head with narrow rostral waist and modest expanded terminal bulb, posterior head wider. Fleshed skull with paired eyes, not exposed temporal fenestrae. Do not substitute short broad unconstricted Simosaurus head.

Pointed slender grasping teeth, a few distinctly larger anterior/maxillary fangs among smaller marginal teeth; modestly open jaws12–18degrees keeps fang-bearing profile inspectable. Total count is simplified, not asserted as specimen dental formula; no saber tusks, no flat crushing plates.

Distinct neck approximately1.5times head centerline length, gradual muscular transition into long ribbed trunk. Gentle lateral bend about10–20degrees, no abrupt snake knot or plesiosaur-length neck. Shape not distinguishable by pose alone.

Four splayed jointed limbs, forelimbs broad proximally with visible elbow/short forearm transition and webbed distal feet; hindlimbs somewhat smaller/slenderer. Five conservative digit tips per foot with shallow intervening clefts and partial webbing inferred, not closed sea-turtle flippers.
Long tapering muscular tail continues axial line, no vertical fish fluke, no dorsal fin or armor shell. High neural spines buried in substantial dorsal soft tissue, not an invented exposed sail.
Restrained gray-brown coloration with lighter underside is artistic inference. Smooth low-poly flesh, no fossil slab/support rods or bare vertebrae.

shape_gate.required_combination: Long constricted fang-bearing head, distinct gently curving neck, jointed webbed four-limb plan and tapering tail, whole animal.
shape_gate.comparison: Simosaurus has broad short unconstricted head and blunt bulbous crowns. Nothosaurus must differ in rostral constriction/long symphysis and pointed prominent teeth, not just name, scale or neck pose. Lariosaurus has more compact short-necked proportions; do not reuse its body ratio.
acceptance: Lateral and perspective clearly show elongate head with obvious long pointed fangs, distinct neck and entire tail.
Top makes snout waist and anterior expansion readable versus broad posterior head; neck bends smoothly, limb web tips separated.
Head-on has bilateral pointed teeth and four-limb arrangement without Simosaurus broad blunt-tooth substitution.
No borrowed other-species giant size, fish tail, sea-turtle flipper, cranial holes or fictitious complete fossil claim.
